back: A duty both spouses carry out together or take turns to do, such as earning income, childcare or deciding on money.
Husband and wife have equal rights and obligations during marriage and when it ends (section 26 of the Constitution).

front: What did the Legal Age of Majority Act (1982) do?
back: Made every person, including women under customary law, a legal adult at 18.

front: Name three indigenous roles of a husband.
back: Any three of: head of household, herding cattle, hunting, building huts and granaries, clearing fields, protecting the family.

front: Name three indigenous roles of a wife.
back: Any three of: planting and harvesting, processing and storing food, cooking, caring for children, teaching girls, caring for the sick.

front: Give four reasons why roles in marriage are changing.
back: Education, employment of women, changes in the law, urbanisation (also religion, the media and economic pressure).
When a spouse (usually a working wife) does paid work and still carries all or most of the unpaid housework.

front: Does equality of spouses mean they do identical tasks?
back: No. It means equal rights and obligations; couples may divide tasks by agreement.
